para.text: Establishment.
There is hereby established as a unit within the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (“DHCD”), the Maryland Housing Innovation Incubator (“Incubator”).

The Incubator shall serve as the State’s housing construction research, development, and innovation hub and shall identify, evaluate, test, and advance transformative solutions to address the underlying causes of Maryland's housing shortage.
DHCD shall designate a Director of the Incubator who shall coordinate and oversee the Incubator’s activities pursuant to this Executive Order.
DHCD may designate other State personnel or contractors to administer and support the Incubator’s activities.
Subject to applicable law, the Incubator may:
Pursue funding opportunities to support its’ programs and activities; and
Receive and administer funding from State appropriations, philanthropic contributions, grants, partnerships, and other lawful funding sources.
Responsibilities. The Incubator shall:

Conduct research and analysis concerning housing production, affordability, land use, permitting, infrastructure, supply chains, construction methods, housing finance, workforce development, and other factors affecting Maryland’s housing supply;

In consultation with the Advisory Council established under Section B of this Executive Order, identify opportunities to modernize, simplify, and improve State and local regulations, policies, and administrative processes affecting housing production and affordability;
Design, implement, and evaluate pilot projects intended to test innovative approaches to housing challenges, including:
Emerging construction technologies;
Innovative construction methods and processes;
Policies or regulatory changes to support adoption of new technologies and methods; and
Innovative financial products and business models;
Ensure pilot programs are designed to produce measurable outcomes and practical findings and recommendations for implementation by State and local governments;
Develop and implement recommendations for scaling successful pilot programs and innovative practices throughout the State;

Develop recommendations concerning regulatory reform, process improvement, administrative modernization, technological innovation, financing tools, workforce development strategies, and other actions intended to increase housing supply and improve housing outcomes;

Subject to available resources and personnel, provide technical assistance, guidance, best practices, model policies, and implementation support to State agencies, local governments, housing providers, and other stakeholders; and
Within six (6) months of the effective date of this Executive Order, launch an initiative to support the expanded deployment of factory-built and modular housing, as described in Section C below.
Collaboration and Partnerships.

The Incubator shall collaborate with the Governor’s Innovation Team and may partner with State agencies, local governments, institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations, research institutions, foundations, industry organizations, private-sector entities, and any other entities or individuals determined to be appropriate.

The Incubator shall provide opportunities for entrepreneurs, researchers, practitioners, and subject matter experts in the construction, real estate, design, technology, infrastructure, finance, planning, and related sectors to collaborate in identifying and advancing innovative housing solutions.

The Incubator may convene or participate in working groups, advisory panels, stakeholder forums, innovation challenges, demonstration projects, and other collaborative initiatives to advance its mission.
Research and Programs.
The Incubator shall engage subject matter experts from a broad range of disciplines to explore innovative solutions to Maryland’s housing supply and affordability challenges.

The Incubator may conduct research, feasibility studies, demonstrations, and pilot programs related to housing policy, development practices, financing tools, regulatory modernization, construction innovation, public-sector process improvement, and other housing-related topics.

The Incubator shall prioritize the housing topics recommended by the Advisory Council established under Section B of this Executive Order, for focused research, policy development, and pilot program implementation.
On at least a quarterly basis, the Incubator shall provide the Advisory Council with a report on its activities, findings, and recommendations for policy reform based on its research and findings.
Reporting. On or before October 1, 2027, and annually thereafter, DHCD shall submit a report to the Governor summarizing the Incubator’s progress, including:
Research activities;
Partnerships and new funding sources established;
Pilot programs launched or completed;
Measurable outcomes of the pilot programs; and
Findings and recommendations.
Establishment.
There is hereby established a Housing Innovation Advisory Council (“Advisory Council”) to:
Identify sources of funding for the Incubator;
Advise and recommend priority topics of study to the Incubator; and

Based on the Incubator’s findings, recommendations, and other relevant information, formalize and advance recommendations for legislative, regulatory, and budgetary actions to address Maryland’s undersupply of housing and resulting high housing costs.
The Advisory Council shall be administered by DHCD in consultation with the Office of the Governor.
Membership.
The Advisory Council shall consist of not fewer than twenty (20) and no more than thirty-two (32) members, as designated below:
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development, or the Secretary's designee;
The Secretary of the Environment, or the Secretary's designee;
The Secretary of Labor, or the Secretary’s designee;
The Secretary of Transportation, or the Secretary's designee;
The Secretary of Planning, or the Secretary's designee;
The Special Secretary of the Governor’s Office for Children, or the Secretary’s designee;
The Comptroller, or the Comptroller's designee;
Three (3) members of the Maryland House of Delegates, appointed by the Speaker of the House;
Three (3) members of the Maryland Senate, appointed by the President of the Senate; and
Additional invitees, at the discretion of the Secretary of Housing and Community Development, to include:
One (1) representative from the Maryland Association of Counties;
One (1) representative from the Maryland Municipal League;
Up to six (6) elected local government officials;
Up to four (4) representatives from housing or construction trade associations;
Up to two (2) representatives from labor unions or other worker-serving organizations;
Up to two (2) representatives from housing advocacy organizations;
Up to two (2) representatives from affordable housing developers;
One (1) representative from a local planning department in the State;
One (1) representative from a local health department in the State;
One (1) representative from a financial institution in the State;
One (1) representative from an institution of higher education in the State; and
Up to two (2) representatives from community stakeholder organizations.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development shall designate the Chair of the Advisory Council.
Administration.
The Advisory Council shall meet as often as its duties require, but no less than quarterly, at the time and place determined by the Chair.
The Chair shall convene and preside over the meetings of the Advisory Council.
The Advisory Council shall hold its first meeting within one hundred twenty (120) calendar days of the effective date of this Executive Order.
The Advisory Council may form ad hoc subcommittees to promote and advance specific legislative, regulatory, or budgetary reforms recommended by the Advisory Council.
The Advisory Council’s ad hoc subcommittees may meet in between the full Advisory Council’s official meetings.
The Advisory Council shall be staffed by DHCD.

Members of the Advisory Council may not receive any compensation for their services but may be reimbursed for reasonable expenses incurred by travel for the performance of their duties, in accordance with the Standard State Travel Regulations, and as provided in the State budget.
Duties. The Advisory Council shall:
On a quarterly basis, identify and recommend to the Incubator potential sources of funding and priority topics for study, research, evaluation, and pilot programs;

Based on the findings and recommendations of the Incubator, develop formal recommendations for legislative, regulatory, and budgetary actions to implement and support the findings and recommendations of the Incubator;
Beginning on July 1, 2027, and biannually thereafter, report to the Governor and the General Assembly on the activities of the Advisory Council, including:
Recommended priority topics for study, research, evaluation, and pilot programs by the Incubator;
The findings and recommendations of the Incubator; and
Any formal recommendations for legislative, regulatory, or budgetary actions resulting from the findings and recommendations of the Incubator; and

Develop recommendations that may address regulatory reform, process improvement, administrative modernization, technological innovation, financing tools, workforce development strategies, and other actions intended to increase the supply of housing and improve housing outcomes in Maryland.

para.heading: Governor’s Initiative to Accelerate Factory-Built Housing Production.

para.text: Establishment.

There is hereby established the Governor's Initiative to Accelerate Factory-Built Housing Production (“Initiative”), to address housing affordability in Maryland by exploring and encouraging the adoption of innovative construction methods, financing tools, and technical assistance.
The Initiative shall be initiated and implemented by DHCD under the auspices of the Maryland Housing Innovation Incubator and in consultation with the Office of the Governor.
Factory-Built Housing Summit.

Within six (6) months of the effective date of this Executive Order, DHCD shall provide funding and technical assistance to support a Factory-Built Housing Summit (“Summit”), to identify barriers to the production, financing, permitting, approval, shipping, and deployment of factory-built and modular housing in Maryland and develop recommendations to increase the use of these housing technologies.
DHCD shall invite stakeholders from the housing, construction, manufacturing, finance, labor, and local government sectors to participate in the Summit.
Within sixty (60) days after the Summit, DHCD shall prepare and publish an Action Plan that recommends:
Administrative, regulatory, legislative, and programmatic actions to accelerate the production and adoption of factory-built and modular housing in Maryland: and
Studies and pilot programs that should be undertaken by the Maryland Housing Innovation Incubator.
Technical Assistance and Support for Local Government.

DHCD, in coordination with the Maryland Department of Planning, shall establish a pilot technical assistance program to assist local governments seeking to modernize zoning, permitting, inspection, and development review processes related to factory-built and modular housing.

DHCD and the Maryland Department of Planning shall identify and disseminate best practices for local governments to streamline approval processes and remove barriers to factory-built and modular housing.

To the extent permitted by law and subject to available funding, DHCD shall evaluate the use of Community Development Block Grant funds and other available grant programs to support local government initiatives that facilitate the production and deployment of factory-built and modular housing.
Modernization of Regulatory Standards.

DHCD, in coordination with the Maryland Department of Labor and other relevant State agencies, shall review existing regulations governing factory-built and modular housing and develop recommendations for amendments to the Code of Maryland Regulations to modernize and streamline standards, inspection procedures, certification requirements, and administrative processes, while maintaining public health, safety, and quality standards.
DHCD shall submit its recommendations regarding the regulatory framework to the Governor by March 1, 2027.
State Framework for Pre-Approved Plans.
DHCD, in consultation with the Maryland Department of Planning, shall develop a framework for the review and approval of standardized modular housing plans that may be utilized throughout Maryland.
The framework shall explore State-level pre-approval of modular housing designs and shall provide guidance to local jurisdictions regarding the recognition and use of approved plans.
To develop the framework, DHCD shall consult with local governments, building officials, modular manufacturers, architects, engineers, and housing providers.
Innovative Financing Strategies.

DHCD shall evaluate and report on barriers, gaps, pain points, and opportunities related to financing and capital stacks for projects involving factory-built or modular housing and identify innovative financing tools and programs that may support the adoption and scaling of factory-built and modular housing in Maryland.

The evaluation should consider financing mechanisms for manufacturers, developers, nonprofit housing providers, local governments, and homebuyers, as well as opportunities to leverage public-private partnerships and federal resources.

DHCD shall identify any legislative, regulatory, or administrative actions necessary to facilitate implementation of viable financing tools and submit its recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by March 1, 2027.

Reporting. On or before July 1, 2028, DHCD shall submit to the Governor a report summarizing activities undertaken pursuant to this Executive Order including progress toward the objectives of the Initiative, the implementation of the Action Plan, and any additional recommendations to accelerate the production and adoption of factory-built and modular housing in Maryland.
Establishment.

DHCD, in coordination with the Maryland Department of Labor, shall establish a Modular Workforce Partnership (“Partnership”) to strengthen and expand the workforce pipeline supporting factory-built and modular housing in Maryland.

The Partnership shall include representatives from State agencies, institutions of higher education, community colleges, trade associations, labor organizations, modular manufacturers, housing developers, workforce development organizations, and other stakeholders as determined appropriate by DHCD and the Department of Labor.
Within DHCD, the Partnership shall be initiated and implemented under the auspices of the Housing Innovation Incubator.
Responsibilities. The Partnership shall:
Evaluate current and projected workforce needs associated with factory-built and modular housing production and deployment in Maryland;
Study and make recommendations regarding workforce training, credentialing, apprenticeship opportunities, and curriculum development necessary to support the growth of the modular housing sector;
Identify opportunities to align existing workforce development programs with the needs of modular manufacturers, contractors, developers, and local governments;
Develop strategies to expand outreach and recruitment for existing training and other workforce development programs related to housing construction; and
Recommend strategies to recruit and retain workers in occupations supporting factory-built and modular housing.
Modular Workforce Academy Framework.

The Partnership shall develop a framework for the establishment of a Modular Workforce Academy to be administered through a participating Maryland institution of higher education including community colleges.
The framework shall address:
Curriculum design and industry-recognized credentials;
Apprenticeship and internship opportunities;
Partnerships with manufacturers, contractors, and housing providers;
Workforce recruitment strategies; and
Opportunities for dual enrollment, continuing education, and incumbent worker training.
The framework shall identify potential funding sources, implementation strategies, and opportunities to leverage existing State workforce development resources.
Maryland Corps/Service Year Option Workforce Opportunities.

DHCD, in collaboration with the Maryland Department of Service & Civic Innovation, and in consultation with the Maryland Department of Labor and other relevant State agencies, shall identify opportunities to incorporate factory-built and modular housing workforce development into the Maryland Corps/Service Year Option Programs.

These efforts shall be coordinated with new and expanded high school-level registered apprenticeship programs and shall involve collaboration with manufacturers, educational institutions, nonprofit organizations, workforce development organizations, housing providers, labor unions, and other worker-serving organizations to create opportunities for participants to receive hands-on training and work experience in housing construction, manufacturing, rehabilitation, and related fields.
Modular Solutions for Vacant Property Redevelopment.

DHCD shall work with the Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Council and other relevant entities to evaluate opportunities to incorporate factory-built and modular housing solutions into existing vacant-property revitalization initiatives.
Such efforts may include incentives, pilot programs, workforce development initiatives, and demonstration projects supporting:
Rehabilitation of vacant properties;
Infill development;
Scattered-site housing development; and
Other neighborhood revitalization efforts.
Special consideration shall be given to projects that create workforce development opportunities for Maryland residents and support local hiring.
Baltimore Modular Training Facility and Demonstration Site.

DHCD shall collaborate with Baltimore City, educational institutions, industry partners, and other stakeholders to develop a plan to establish a modular construction training facility and demonstration site within Baltimore City.

The plan shall identify potential locations, partnership structures, funding opportunities, workforce development benefits, and opportunities to coordinate with housing construction innovation initiatives operating within the State.
DHCD shall report its findings and recommendations to the Governor, the General Assembly, and the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore.
Employer and Training Program Assistance.

DHCD, the Maryland Department of Labor, and Maryland Department of Planning shall identify opportunities to provide incentives, technical assistance, and other support to employers, educational institutions, apprenticeship programs, and workforce development providers seeking to expand or adapt training programs to support factory-built and modular housing occupations.
Such assistance may include support related to:
Manufacturing and construction skills;
Digital design and production technologies;
Supply chain and logistics management;
Building inspection and code compliance;
Permitting and development review processes;
Land use planning and development administration; and
Other occupations necessary to support the factory-built and modular housing industry.

Reporting. On or before July 1, 2028, DHCD and the Maryland Department of Labor shall submit a joint report to the Governor summarizing actions taken pursuant to this Executive Order including the progress of the Partnership, development of the Modular Workforce Academy, and recommending any additional measures necessary to strengthen Maryland's factory-built and modular housing workforce pipeline.

This Executive Order shall be implemented in a manner that is consistent with all applicable statutes and regulations. Nothing in this Executive Order shall operate to contravene any State or federal law or to affect the State's receipt of federal funding.

If any provision of this Executive Order or its application to any person, entity, or circumstance is held invalid by any court of competent jurisdiction, all other provisions or applications of the Executive Order shall remain in effect to the extent possible without the invalid provision or application. To achieve this purpose, the provisions of this Executive Order are severable.

section.heading: State of Maryland Workplace Substance Misuse Policy

para.heading: Scope.
para.text: This policy applies to all individuals employed by the Executive Branch of the Maryland State Government.

para.heading: Definitions.
para.text: The following words have the meanings indicated:
“Alcohol” means any form of ethanol, or any beverage or substance containing ethanol.
“Alcohol-Related Offense” means a crime that requires alcohol possession or consumption as an element of the offense.

“Cannabis” means the plant Cannabis Sativa L. and any part of the plant, including all derivatives, extracts, cannabinoids, isomers, acids, salts, and salts of isomers, whether growing or not, with a delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol concentration greater than 0.3% on a dry weight basis. Cannabis includes cannabis products but does not include hemp or hemp products as defined by § 14–101 of the Agriculture Article.

“Cannabis-Related Offense” means any crime that involves the use, sale, possession, distribution, dispensation, manufacture, or transfer of cannabis under Md. Code Ann., Crim. Law §§ 5-101 through 5-1101, excluding civil use offenses set forth in Crim. Law 5-601(c)(2)(ii).

“Controlled Dangerous Substance” means any substance, excluding cannabis, that is controlled under the Federal Controlled Substances Act, 21 U.S.C. § 801, et seq., as amended, and/or the Maryland Controlled Dangerous Substances Act, Md. Code Ann., Crim. Law §§ 5-101 through 5-1101.
“Controlled Dangerous Substance Offense” means:
A controlled dangerous substance violation, under Md. Code Ann., Crim. Law §§ 5-101 through 5-1101;
An offense of the law of any other jurisdiction if the prohibited conduct would be a controlled dangerous substance violation if committed in this State;
Driving or attempting to drive while under the influence of a controlled dangerous substance under Md. Code Ann., Transp. § 21-902; or
Operating or attempting to operate a vessel while impaired by a controlled dangerous substance under Md. Code Ann., Nat. Res. § 8-738.
“Conviction” means:
A judgment of conviction, whether entered upon a finding of guilt or acceptance of a guilty plea or plea of nolo contendere, and the imposition of sentence; or
The staying of the entry of judgment and the placing of the defendant on probation after a finding of guilty or the acceptance of a plea of nolo contendere.

“Drug” means any controlled dangerous substance, non-prescription drug, or prescription drug, taken into the body, which may impair one’s mental faculties and/or change one’s mood and/or physical performance.
“Drug-Related Offenses” means:
Crimes listed under the Maryland Controlled Dangerous Substances Act, Md. Code Ann., Crim. Law §§ 5-101 through 5-1101.
Driving or attempting to drive while under the influence of drugs or drugs and alcohol under Md. Code Ann., Transp. § 21-902.
Operating or attempting to operate a vessel while under the influence of drugs or drugs and alcohol under Md. Code Ann., Nat. Res. § 8-738.
“Employee” means:
A merit-protected (classified), at will (unclassified), contractual, key employee, or other employee or official in the Executive Branch;
A volunteer who provides a service to or for a unit in the Executive Branch; or
A member of a Board or Commission in the Executive Branch.
“Impaired” means reduced cognitive or physical ability that results from use of drugs, alcohol, cannabis, or controlled dangerous substances.
“Intoxicating Cannabinoid” means a product intended for human consumption or inhalation that contains more than 0.5 milligrams of tetrahydrocannabinol per serving.
“Medical Cannabis” means all parts of any plant of the genus cannabis, whether growing or not, including:
The seeds of the plant;
The resin extracted from any part of the plant; and

Any compound, manufacture, salt, derivative, mixture, or preparation of the plant, its seeds, or resin including tetrahydrocannabinol and all other naturally produced cannabinoid derivatives, whether produced directly or indirectly by extraction.
Medical cannabis does not include:
Hemp, as defined in Md. Code Ann., Agric. § 14-101;
Mature stalks of the plant or fiber produced from the mature stalks;
Oil or cake made from the seeds of the plant;
Any other compound, manufacture, salt, derivative, mixture, or preparation of the mature stalks, fiber, oil, or cake; or
The sterilized seed of the plant that is incapable of germination.
“Non-Prescription Drug” means any over-the-counter drug that is available without a written prescription by an authorized medical professional.
“Prescription Drug” means a drug that may be dispensed only on the prescription of a health practitioner who is authorized by law to prescribe the drug
“Safety-Sensitive Employee” means an employee who operates heavy machinery and includes, but are not limited to, an operator of a crane, winch, or top loader and a driver of hustler or forklift.

“Sensitive Employee” means an employee whose classification or position has been designated sensitive by the Secretary of Budget and Management or the Secretary's designated representative, or the employee’s appointing authority.

“Sensitive Classification” means a classification in which the Secretary of Budget and Management or the Secretary's designated representative has determined that any of the following conditions exists:

An employee in the classification has a substantially significant degree of responsibility for the safety of others and there is a potential that impaired performance of the employee could result in death of or injury to the employee or others;
An employee in the classification is required to carry a firearm;
An employee in the classification is directly involved in efforts to interdict the flow of narcotics; or
An employee in the classification is directly involved with narcotics law enforcement.

“Sensitive Position” means a position for which an appointing authority has determined that any of the conditions listed in Section B (18) of this executive order exists, but which is not in a sensitive classification.
“Substance” means alcohol, drugs, or cannabis.
“Substance Misuse” means:
The use of an illegal drug that results in workplace impairment and/or impaired job performance;
The intentional misuse of any legal drug that results in workplace impairment and/or impaired job performance;

The intentional use of any prescription drug in a manner inconsistent with its medically prescribed, intended use, or under circumstances where its use is not permitted, that results in workplace impairment and/or impaired job performance;
The use of alcohol where such use results in workplace impairment and/or impairs job performance; or
The use of cannabis where such use results in workplace impairment and/or impairs job performance.
“Workplace” means any place where an employee is performing work for the State of Maryland.
“Work Time” means time during which an employee:
Is on duty, whether at the employee’s principal work site or at a remote location as part of the State's telework program;
Participates in training activities as a job assignment;
Is on the employer's premises and is on call and waiting for work;
Is not on the employer's premises, but is on call and waiting for work, and the employee's personal activities are substantially restricted;
Is changing into and removing program-specified clothing and equipment necessary for the performance of the job;
Participates in activities that are job-related immediately before the beginning or immediately after the end of an assigned shift;
Travels to and from work after being recalled to work by the appointing authority or the appointing authority's designated representative after the employee has completed the standard workday;

Travels to and from work after being called to work by the appointing authority or the appointing authority's designated representative on the employee's scheduled day off if the employee works fewer than 8 hours as a result of being called on the employee's scheduled day off; or
Travels between home and a work site other than the assigned office, in accordance with the Standard Travel Regulations.
Work time includes any other time defined as work time under the Fair Labor Standards Act, 29 U.S.C. § 201 et seq., if applicable.

para.heading: General Policy.
para.text: The State of Maryland establishes the following Substance Misuse Policy for the Executive Branch of State Government:
All employees in the workplace must be capable of performing their duties. An employee shall not report to work, or spend any work time, in an unfit condition to perform their duties.
Substance misuse by any employee is prohibited at all times.
Employees experiencing substance use problems are encouraged to seek assistance through:
Their employer;
Self-referral to the state administered Employee Assistance Program (“EAP”);
Self-referral to the MyMDCares program or similar state-sponsored assistance program; or
Self-referral to an alternative certified rehabilitation program.

An employee shall not report to work, or spend any work time, under the influence of alcohol, cannabis, intoxicating cannabinoids or controlled dangerous substances. Any employee who reports to work, or spends any work time, with their mental or physical abilities impaired by alcohol, cannabis, or controlled dangerous substances, is in violation of this policy and shall be subject to disciplinary action.

Employees may not consume alcohol or controlled dangerous substances or consume, smoke, or otherwise ingest cannabis or intoxicating cannabinoid or controlled substances on State property, at any worksite, or during work hours or while on work time. This conduct is also prohibited for employees on official business, whether on or off State Property.

The unlawful manufacture, distribution, dispensation, possession, or use of cannabis, intoxicating cannabinoids or controlled substances is prohibited on State property, at any worksite, or during work hours or while on work time.

Employees are prohibited from consuming and/or being under the influence of alcohol, cannabis, an intoxicating cannabinoid, or a controlled dangerous substance while operating State equipment, vehicles, or other property.
Employees are prohibited from committing offenses related to alcohol, cannabis, intoxicating cannabinoids or controlled dangerous substances.

Employees who plead guilty, accept a plea of nolo contendere, receive a probation before judgment, or are convicted of an offense relating to alcohol, cannabis, intoxicating cannabinoids or controlled dangerous substances are in violation of this policy and must report the disposition of the case to their supervisor and/or appointing authority no later than five (5) workdays after the disposition.

para.heading: Medical Cannabis.
para.text: Employees who are registered and certified medical cannabis patients may not possess, consume, smoke, or otherwise ingest cannabis on State property, at any worksite or during work time.

Employees who are registered and certified medical cannabis patients are responsible for consulting the certifying provider to ascertain whether the medical cannabis will interfere with the safe performance of their job duties.

If the use of any medical cannabis could compromise an employee's performance or the safety of the employee, fellow employees, or the public, it is the employee's responsibility to notify their supervisor and/or appointing authority and use appropriate leave to avoid unsafe work practices.

para.heading: Prescription & Over-The-Counter Drugs.
para.text: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs must be taken in standard dosage and/or according to a physician’s prescription.

Employees who take prescribed or over-the-counter medications are responsible for consulting the prescribing physician and/or pharmacist to ascertain whether the medication will interfere with the safe performance of their job duties.

If the use of any prescription or over-the counter drug could compromise an employee's performance or the safety of the employee, fellow employees, or the public, it is the employee's responsibility to notify their supervisor and/or appointing authority and use appropriate leave to avoid unsafe work practices.

An employee shall not report to work, or spend any work time, under the inappropriate influence of prescription or over-the-counter drugs. Any employee who reports to work, or spends any work time, with their mental or physical abilities inappropriately impaired by prescription or over-the-counter drugs is in violation of this policy and shall be subject to disciplinary action.

para.heading: Sanctions for Non-Sensitive and Non-Safety Sensitive Employees.

para.text: A non-sensitive or non-safety sensitive employee who violates the Substance Misuse Policy as described in Section D shall:
On the first instance be referred to the state-administered EAP and subject to any other appropriate disciplinary actions;

On the second instance, at a minimum, be suspended for at least five (5) days, be referred to the state-administered EAP, be required to participate successfully in a state-approved treatment program, and be subject to any other appropriate disciplinary actions, up to and including termination;
On the third instance, be terminated.

para.heading: Sanctions for Sensitive and Safety-Sensitive Employees.

para.text: A sensitive or safety-sensitive employee shall be suspended for fifteen (15) days and required to successfully participate in a state- approved substance use treatment program designated by the state- administered EAP the first time and subject to progressive action upon subsequent offenses where the employee is:
Convicted of an at-the-workplace offense related to alcohol, cannabis or controlled dangerous substances; or
Found under the influence of alcohol, cannabis or controlled dangerous substances while at the workplace.
A sensitive or safety-sensitive employee convicted of an out-of-workplace offense related to alcohol, cannabis or controlled dangerous substances shall:
On the first conviction be referred to the state-administered EAP and subject to any other appropriate disciplinary actions;

On the second conviction, at a minimum, be suspended for at least five (5) days, be referred the state-administered EAP, be required to participate successfully in a state approved treatment program, and be subject to any other appropriate disciplinary actions, up to and including termination;
On the third conviction, be terminated.

A sensitive or safety-sensitive employee who tests positive for a controlled dangerous substance as a result of a random drug test shall be suspended for five (5) workdays and be required to successfully participate in a drug treatment program approved by the state, as provided for by the appointing authority's drug testing protocol. Employees may be subject to progressive discipline upon subsequent offenses.
A sensitive or safety-sensitive employee who misuses, at work or on work time, a legally prescribed drug or an over-the-counter drug shall:
On the first instance be referred to the state-administered EAP and subject to any other appropriate disciplinary actions;

On the second instance, at a minimum, be suspended for at least five (5) days, be referred to the state-administered EAP, be required to participate successfully in a treatment program, and be subject to any other appropriate disciplinary actions, up to and including termination;
On the third instance, be terminated.

An employee may request referral to the state-administered EAP for access to confidential professional assistance for substance use problems or may self-refer to the MyMDCares program or similar state-sponsored assistance program to receive confidential professional assistance.

Employees will not face disciplinary action solely for requesting referral to the state-administered EAP or voluntarily obtaining other assistance and/or treatment for a substance use problem. The State of Maryland encourages any employee who needs such assistance and treatment to seek and obtain it. However, participation in a treatment or recovery program will neither relieve employees from the requirement of satisfactory job performance, nor insulate them from termination or adverse personnel actions for failing to comply with any of the State’s policies and procedures.

Substance misuse-related disciplinary actions, up to and including termination, may be, but do not have to be, held in abeyance pending an employee’s completion of an assistance and treatment program approved by the State. The option of holding a disciplinary action in abeyance is not an employee entitlement or right but is a privilege to be granted at the discretion of the appointing authority, in consultation with the Department of Budget and Management, or the individual responsible for Human Resources for the respective State agency under appropriate circumstances.

The Secretary of Budget and Management and the head of every other personnel system in the Executive Branch shall adopt such policies and regulations as are necessary or desirable for the implementation of this Executive Order.
All appointing authorities and supervisory employees are responsible for implementing, enforcing, and monitoring compliance with the requirements of this Executive Order.
All employees are required to acknowledge receipt of a copy of this Executive Order by returning an acknowledgement of receipt to their supervisor for insertion in their personnel file.

Agencies with employees that are subject to other regulations or rules related to employee substance misuse and out of workplace use of drugs or cannabis are exempt from the conflicting requirements in this policy.
If a supervisor or appointing authority observes any signs of possible substance misuse in any employee during working hours, this shall constitute reasonable grounds for an investigation.

If a non-supervisory employee observes any signs of possible substance misuse in any employee during working hours and reports it to a supervisor or appointing authority, this shall constitute reasonable grounds for an investigation.

A supervisor and/or appointing authority, on observing such signs or receiving a report, in consultation with the Department of Budget and Management, or the individual responsible for Human Resources for the respective State agency, should investigate by appropriate measures.

If the supervisory investigation supports a conclusion of substance misuse by the investigated employee(s), the supervisor and/or appointing authority shall consult the Department of Budget and Management, the individual responsible for Human Resources for the respective State agency, or the State Medical Director to determine the appropriate next steps, which may include testing.

When an appointing authority learns or based on observation or reliable information, suspects that an employee has committed an alcohol-related offense, cannabis-related offense, controlled dangerous substance offense, or other drug-related offense, the appointing authority shall refer the matter to the appropriate law enforcement authority for further investigation and prosecution.
All employees shall cooperate fully with law enforcement authorities in the investigation and prosecution of suspected criminal violations.

para.heading: Employee Education.
para.text: All appointing authorities shall educate and inform their employees about:
The dangers of drug and alcohol misuse in the workplace;
The State of Maryland's policy of maintaining a drug-free and recovery-friendly workplace;
Any drug and alcohol misuse counseling, rehabilitation, and the state-administered EAP that is available; and
The penalties that may be imposed upon employees for violations of this Executive Order.
This policy does not constitute or create an express or implied contract. It is not intended to, and does not, create contractual obligations with respect to any matter it covers.

This Executive Order shall be implemented in a manner that is consistent with all applicable statutes and regulations. Nothing in this Executive Order shall operate to contravene any State or federal law or to affect the State's receipt of federal funding.
If a State entity is subject to a federal law or regulation that conflicts with this Executive Order, the federal law or regulation shall take precedence.

If any provision of this Executive Order or its application to any person, entity, or circumstance is held invalid by any court of competent jurisdiction, all other provisions or applications of the Executive Order shall remain in effect to the extent possible without the invalid provision or application. To achieve this purpose, the provisions of this Executive Order are severable.

para.text: Chesapeake Bay and Its Tidal Tributaries.
Quota. The annual target harvest for the commercial fishery is 42.5 percent of the overall Maryland quota.
Size Limits.
The minimum legal size for the commercial fishery is 18 inches total length.
The maximum legal size for the commercial fishery is 36 inches total length.
Seasons. The commercial seasons for taking striped bass for permittees registered in the Chesapeake Bay individual transferrable quota fishery are as follows:
The haul seine season is June 1 through the last day of February;
The hook and line season is June 1 through December 31;
The pound net season is June 1 through December 31; and
The drift gill net season is December 1 through the last day of February.
The Secretary shall allocate the annual target harvest for the following fisheries:
Chesapeake Bay Individual Transferrable Quota; and
Atlantic Ocean, its coastal bays and their tidal tributaries.
Initial Calculation of Shares in the Fisheries of the Chesapeake Bay and Its Tidal Tributaries.

A tidal fish licensee with a striped bass permit registered in the Chesapeake Bay and its tidal tributaries as of May 10, 2013 shall receive a share of the striped bass fishery in accordance with this section.
Pound Net and Haul Seine.
The amount of shares to be divided among the pound net and haul seine fisheries is 33 percent of the Chesapeake Bay commercial quota.
Tidal fish licensees with a striped bass permit registered in the pound net fishery as of May 10, 2013 shall each receive an equal share.

Tidal fish licensees with a striped bass permit registered in the haul seine fishery as of May 10, 2013 shall each receive a share equal to the amount of one third of the share assigned to a striped bass permit registered in the pound net fishery as of May 10, 2013.
Gill Net and Hook and Line.
The amount of shares to be divided among the gill net and hook and line fisheries is 67 percent of the overall commercial quota.

Each tidal fish licensee with a striped bass permit registered in either the gill net or hook and line fisheries as of May 10, 2013 shall receive an equal share of 25 percent of the gill net and hook and line quota.

In addition to the initial baseline share described in §A(6)(c)(ii) of this regulation, each tidal fish licensee with a striped bass permit registered in either the gill net or hook and line fisheries as of May 10, 2013 may receive additional shares of the remaining 75 percent of the gill net and hook and line quota based on the average poundage of the striped bass harvested by the permittee during the period January 1, 2001 through February 29, 2012.
The Secretary may:
Reassign a commercial tidal fish licensee's allocation if the licensee has not registered for the allocation;
Modify the allocation of all commercial tidal fish licensees during the season;
Consider an appeal of the initial calculation of shares in the fisheries of the Chesapeake Bay and its tidal tributaries under §A(6) of this regulation; and
Modify the shares of all commercial tidal fish licensees in an equal manner prior to the beginning of the quota year.

A flag specified by the Department shall be displayed on the vessel at least 3 feet above the surface on which it is mounted and clearly visible to approaching vessels if the individuals on board are engaged in commercial striped bass fishing to denote whether the individuals on board are participating in the Chesapeake Bay individual transferrable quota fishery.
Harvest of Species Other Than Striped Bass — Drift Gill Net.

An individual participating in the drift gill net fishery in accordance with §C(2) of this regulation may harvest species of fish other than striped bass from the drift gill net if the permittee possesses the required remaining allocation set by the public notice issued in accordance with this section.
A striped bass permittee harvesting fish in accordance with this section shall follow all rules and regulations for the species harvested.
Public Notice.

The Secretary shall establish and may modify the remaining allocation required for a permittee to take species other than striped bass as described in §C(8)(a) of this regulation by issuing a public notice on the Department’s website.
The public notice shall state its effective hour and date and shall be published on the Department’s website at least 48 hours in advance of the effective hour and date.

The Secretary shall make a reasonable effort to disseminate a public notice issued under this section through various other media so that an affected individual has a reasonable opportunity to be informed.
A violation of the restrictions set by the Secretary in accordance with this section is a violation of this regulation.
Atlantic Ocean, its Coastal Bays and Their Tributaries.
Quota. The annual target harvest for the commercial fishery is the quota set by the Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission.
Minimum Size. The minimum legal size for the commercial fishery is 24 inches.
Season. The commercial season for the taking of striped bass for all gears is October 1 through May 31.
A striped bass caught in the waters of the State shall be landed in the State.

The Department may waive the provisions set forth in §B(4) of this regulation if an individual files with the Department an affidavit signed by the individual which specifies the out-of-State landing location and Maryland check station where fish will be counted and weighed.

The Secretary may modify the number of licensees with individual permits that may catch striped bass on a boat on any day by publishing notice in a daily newspaper of general circulation at least 48 hours in advance of the time of modification, stating the effective hour and date.
Initial Calculation of Shares in the Atlantic Ocean, Its Coastal Bays, and Their Tidal Tributaries.

A tidal fish licensee with a striped bass permit registered in the Atlantic Ocean, its coastal bays, and their tidal tributaries shall receive a share of the striped bass fishery in accordance with this section.
A tidal fish licensee shall receive an equal share for each of their permits registered in the Atlantic Ocean fishery.
A tidal fish licensee may receive a maximum share equal to four permits registered in the Atlantic Ocean fishery.
Drift Gill Net Fishery Limitations.
The provisions of this section apply to a commercial tidal fish licensee participating in a striped bass gill net season.
In the tidal waters of the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries:
Only attended drift gill nets, as defined in COMAR 08.02.25.01B, with a stretched mesh size of not less than 5 inches or greater than 7 inches are permitted for the taking of striped bass;
The total length of drift gill net aboard a boat may not exceed 3,500 yards and may not be contained in more than ten containers;
A gill net may not be used to harvest fish or possessed aboard a vessel, unless the gill net has:
Each marker, cork, or float marked with the licensee's commercial tidal fish number; or
A float line with a marker permanently affixed every 50 feet bearing the licensee's commercial tidal fish number; and
A drift gill net may be used on a Saturday or Sunday.
A person may possess and use other legal fishing equipment to catch other fish species while fishing for striped bass with gear as provided in §C(2)(a) of this regulation.
A drift gill net may not be set before 3 a.m. and shall be retrieved and in the boat by 6 p.m.
Flag Marker — Chesapeake Bay or Atlantic Ocean.

A drift gill net set in the Chesapeake Bay or Atlantic Ocean shall be marked, by the licensee, at one end by a square flag measuring at least 144 square inches, supported by a staff sufficient to maintain the flag bottom at least 3 feet above the surface of the water.
The end of a gill net opposite the flag marker shall be marked by either a triangular flag of at least 144 square inches or a floating marker with a volume of at least 460 cubic inches.
Each flag or floating marker shall be marked with the licensee's commercial tidal fish license number.

Flag Marker Tributaries. A drift gill net set in tributaries of the Chesapeake Bay or Atlantic coastal bays and their tributaries shall be marked by the licensee at each end with a floating marker with a volume of at least 460 cubic inches, each bearing the licensee's commercial tidal fish license number, or a flag according to §A(8) of this regulation.

Gill Net and Gill Net Reels — Chesapeake Bay and Its Tidal Tributaries. Except during the commercial striped bass gill net season as specified in §A of this regulation or disseminated by public notice in accordance with Regulation .12H of this chapter, an individual may not catch and possess striped bass if a gill net or gill net reel is aboard the vessel.
Harvest of Species Other Than Striped Bass — Drift Gill Net.

An individual participating in the drift gill net fishery in accordance with §C(2) of this regulation may harvest species of fish other than striped bass from the drift gill net if the permittee possesses the required remaining allocation set by the public notice issued in accordance with this section.
A striped bass permittee harvesting fish in accordance with this section shall follow all rules and regulations for the species harvested.
Public Notice.

The Secretary shall establish and may modify the remaining allocation required for a permittee to take species other than striped bass as described in §C(8)(a) of this regulation by issuing a public notice on the Department’s website.
The public notice shall state its effective hour and date and shall be published on the Department’s website at least 48 hours in advance of the effective hour and date.

The Secretary shall make a reasonable effort to disseminate a public notice issued under this section through various other media so that an affected individual has a reasonable opportunity to be informed.
A violation of the restrictions set by the Secretary in accordance with this section is a violation of this regulation.
Commercial Hook and Line Fishery Limitations. While using commercial hook and line, a person may not catch or attempt to catch striped bass:
Between 1 hour after sunset and 1 hour before sunrise; or
At any time on a Saturday or Sunday.
Pound Net Fishery Limitations.
A commercial tidal fish licensee may not harvest striped bass from a pound net between 6 p.m. and 12 a.m.
A commercial tidal fish licensee may not harvest striped bass from a pound net on Sunday.
A commercial tidal fish licensee shall comply with all additional requirements in the pound net fishery as described in COMAR 08.02.25.07.53
General.
A commercial tidal fish licensee may not catch striped bass between 6 p.m. Friday and 5 a.m. Monday, except as provided in §§C, D, and E of this regulation.
Atlantic Tolerance.

A commercial tidal fish licensee registered in the Atlantic fishery is not in violation of this chapter if their landings do not exceed their allocation by more than the tolerance described in §F(2)(b) of this regulation.

The tolerance for the Atlantic fishery is the greater of either 50 pounds or 4 percent of the remaining allocation available to the permit holder on the final trip when the allocation is fully harvested.
A commercial tidal fish licensee registered in the Chesapeake Bay individual transferable quota fishery who exceeds their allocation by 50 pounds or less is not in violation of this chapter.

If a commercial tidal fish licensee registered in the Chesapeake Bay individual transferable quota or Atlantic fishery exceeds the licensees allocation, that overage may be deducted from the allocation the licensee receives in the next practicable quota year.

If a commercial tidal fish licensee registered in the Chesapeake Bay individual transferable quota fishery accumulates 10 or more points for offenses specific to the striped bass fishery as described in COMAR 08.02.13.02 and .03, that licensee shall be suspended for one quota year.
A commercial tidal fish licensee may catch striped bass using only the striped bass permit assigned to the licensee.

Statements made under oath showing the applicant's education, including the applicant's official college transcript, which reflects completion of a program accredited by the Society of American Foresters and approved by the Board, including:
An undergraduate degree in forestry; or
A comparable graduate or international degree in forestry as set forth in Business Occupations and Professions Article, §7-304(b)(2), Annotated Code of Maryland;

A detailed summary of the applicant's experience in practicing forestry that was obtained after the completion of the educational requirements under Business Occupations and Professions Article, §7-304(b), Annotated Code of Maryland; and
At least five signed references to indicate endorsement of the applicant, of which three or more shall be foresters having personal or professional knowledge of the applicant's forestry experience.
